BiblicalUsage: Naqa means to feel aversion, for the mind to be alienated from someone, and it is used for God's own mind turning from faithless Judah. In Ezekiel 23:18 the Lord says His mind was alienated from Oholibah, like as His mind was alienated from her sister, and in Ezekiel 23:22 He will raise up her lovers against her, from whom her mind is alienated.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that alienation is the saddest word in Ezekiel, because it is God saying His mind has turned from His own people; the lovers she chased are the ones who will come against her, and the turning away is complete.
